title: Dynamics 365 Business Central
description: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central: a company's customers, vendors, items, sales and purchase documents, general ledger — through its API v2.0, signed in as an app of your Microsoft Entra.

fields.name: tenant
fields.label: Tenant
fields.help: Your Microsoft Entra tenant: its directory (tenant) ID or its domain. Pasting Business Central's address from your browser works too.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: The secret's value (not its ID), as it was shown when it was made.

fields.name: environment
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: The environment's name, as in Business Central's address after the tenant (production, sandbox, …).

fields.name: company
fields.label: Company
fields.help: The company to read, by its name or id; none needed when there is only one. The check lists them.

setup.title: An app in Microsoft Entra
setup.say:
Superatom signs in to Business Central as an app of your organisation's own. As an administrator, in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com):

(1) Applications → App registrations → New registration: name it Superatom, Accounts in this organizational directory only, no redirect URI; Register. Copy its Application (client) ID and its Directory (tenant) ID.

(2) API permissions → Add a permission → Dynamics 365 Business Central → Application permissions → API.ReadWrite.All; Add permissions; then Grant admin consent. (Business Central has no read-only permission here: what the app may do is limited inside Business Central, in the next step.)

(3) Certificates & secrets → New client secret → Add; copy its Value at once (it is shown only now).

The check asks Microsoft Entra for the app's token.

fix.say: Microsoft Entra knows no app with that client ID in this tenant. Copy the Application (client) ID again, and check the tenant is the one the app was registered in.
The client secret was refused: it is wrong or has expired. Copy the secret's Value (not its Secret ID), or make a new one under Certificates & secrets.
No such tenant. Give the Directory (tenant) ID from the app's Overview, or the tenant's domain (contoso.onmicrosoft.com).

setup.title: Let the app read, in Business Central
setup.say:
In Business Central, as an administrator: search (Alt+Q) for Microsoft Entra Applications → New. Client ID: {clientId}. Description: Superatom. State: Enabled. Under User Permission Sets add D365 READ (leave Company empty for every company, or name one). Grant Consent if it asks. This is what makes the app read-only.

Then give the environment's name — as in Business Central's address after the tenant (production unless yours is named otherwise). The check signs in and lists the companies.

copy.label: Find the page in Business Central

fix.say: Business Central does not let the app in yet: add it on the Microsoft Entra Applications page with the client ID {clientId}, set its State to Enabled, and give it the D365 READ permission set.
There is no environment by that name. Give its name as in Business Central's address after the tenant (https://businesscentral.dynamics.com/<tenant>/<environment>).
The app signs in but may not read. Give it the D365 READ permission set on the Microsoft Entra Applications page (for every company, or the one to read).

setup.title: Which company
setup.say: Name the company to read, as Business Central shows it — none needed when there is only one. The check lists the environment's companies.

fix.say: Copy one company's name from the list shown.
